sentences: The source asks how many local queries are needed to distinguish high-value from low-value Max-CSP instances.
Its target covers every predicate family \(\Gamma\) and every completeness–soundness pair c,s in the bounded-degree model.
A tester sees only a small portion of an instance, so global unsatisfiability must be reflected in accessible local evidence.
A classification would map the boundary between sublinear testing and problems requiring much broader inspection.
The saved statement does not reproduce the degree-oracle conventions or admissible gap parameters, which are necessary to assign exact query complexities.
